title: Davinci the Dualist: the mind-body divide in large language models and in human learners
benchmark_measurement: The study measured the models' tendency towards intuitive mind-body dualism, specifically probing whether models believe psychological traits (especially epistemic states like thoughts) are distinct from the physical body. This was tested by asking if traits would manifest in the brain and, crucially, if they would persist after death (in an 'afterlife' scenario), a concept central to many religious and faith-based beliefs about the soul.
findings: The more advanced model, GPT-3.5, learned a component of human dualist bias, considering thoughts less likely to manifest in the brain. However, unlike humans who often believe in the persistence of consciousness, GPT-3.5 uniformly responded 'no' to questions about traits persisting in an afterlife. This indicates that while the model could learn the mind-body distinction from text data, it did not acquire the related human intuition or belief in a soul/consciousness that persists after bodily death.
